chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: How Curran pushed Hodes into writing
summary: Hodes says Dale Curran got him to write by telling him to write as he talks. He says every step forward was someone poking him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, you're one of the few musicians who write, and write very well. How did you get into that?
By force. Curran got me involved. He says, all you have to do is sit down and if it needs help,

I'll help you. Write something about your life. Just like you're playing, talk. Just like you're talking, write. So he -- every move I've made that has advanced me is somebody jabbing me in the ass to go forward. It's like a very religious -- I don't think that's a good word, a spiritual priest I met once, I says to him, how come that you have become so tuned in on this stuff? He says, it's from doing that, and he pointed down, like the devil, that I'm doing this. Somebody just poked me and poked me --

With a pitchfork so I went in the other direction. Well, it's the same thing. I was poked to write. I didn't one day get up and say, I'm going to be a writer, a jazz writer. Robert Allen Arthur? says of the two musicians that are writing, I was one of the two, the other he says was Louis Armstrong that he cared to read. He wouldn't care to read any other. And he's a writer.

So I feel complimented by it. It doesn't turn my head too much, because I realize that I better stick to playing music. I'm not going to make it writing. But it's good. I think the musician who can be audible should be, should say it. But don't get involved, don't suddenly think you've become a writer. You're a writer of a subject that you know something about. And if you can stick to that, you'll do well. And to the extent that well can be done doing that, that's fine.
